title: Fine saturated log schemes, log regularity and saturated log blowups
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth]. A log structure on $X$ is a sheaf of commutative monoids $M$ on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with a homomorphism $\alpha:M\to(\mathcal O_X,\cdot)$ such that $\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_X^\times)\to\mathcal O_X^\times$ is an isomorphism. A chart $P\to M$ means that the log structure associated to $P\to\mathcal O_X$ is $M$: at a geometric point with strict local ring $A$, the induced map $P\oplus_{\alpha^{-1}(A^\times)} A^\times\to M_{\bar x}$ is an isomorphism. A monoid $P$ is fine saturated if it is finitely generated, embeds in its group completion, and $ng\in P$ with $g\in P^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ implies $g\in P$. A fine saturated (fs) log scheme is $(X,M,\alpha)$ with etale-local charts by such monoids. Its characteristic monoid is $\overline M_{\bar x}=M_{\bar x}/A^\times$, and its triviality locus is the set where $\overline M_{\bar x}=0$. It is log regular when, for the ideal $I_{\bar x}\subset A$ generated by images of nonunits of $M_{\bar x}$, $A/I_{\bar x}$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $\dim A=\dim(A/I_{\bar x})+\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbf Z}\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ at every geometric point. This is the condition used for the divisorial structure in [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

A morphism $(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ consists of a scheme morphism $f:Y\to X$ and a homomorphism $f^{-1}M\to N$ compatible with the structure maps to $\mathcal O_Y$. A nonempty coherent log ideal $\mathcal I\subset M$ is a subsheaf satisfying $\mathcal I M\subset\mathcal I$, which in an etale-local chart $P\to M$ is generated by a nonempty finite set of elements of $P$. Its pullback to $(Y,N)$ is the ideal generated by its image in $N$; it is invertible if etale locally it is generated by one element of $N$. A saturated log blowup of $(X,M)$ along $\mathcal I$ means an fs log scheme $b:(X',M')\to(X,M)$ whose pulled-back log ideal is invertible, such that every fs log morphism $f:(Y,N)\to(X,M)$ with invertible pulled-back ideal factors uniquely through $b$. The term denotes this universal property; existence is a theorem. A finite saturated log blowup tower is a finite sequence of these morphisms, allowing the sequence of length zero.
